robocup.title: Autonomous Mobile Manipulation at RoboCup@Work 2021
robocup.subtitle: 3D Computer Vision (PCL) & Robotic Grasping with UR3e Collaborative Arm
robocup.author: Lukas Kraus

sections.heading: My Engineering Role & Core Responsibilities
sections.content: As a core robotics engineer in the newly formed university Team SWOT at FHWS (University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt), I was specifically responsible for the two critical manipulation pillars:
list: 3D Vision & Object Recognition (PCL): Designing, implementing, and calibrating the complete 3D perception pipeline using the Point Cloud Library (PCL) and an eye-in-hand Intel RealSense D435i depth camera mounted on the gripper flange.

Robotic Arm Manipulation & Autonomous Grasping: Developing the 6-DoF trajectory planning, inverse kinematics, and precision grasping algorithms for the Universal Robots UR3e collaborative arm equipped with a Robotiq Hand-E parallel gripper using ROS and cartesian_ros_control.

sections.heading: About the RoboCup@Work League
sections.content: The RoboCup@Work league is a premier international benchmark competition in autonomous robotics designed to accelerate applied research for Industry 4.0 and smart manufacturing. Mobile robots must autonomously navigate factory floors, locate dynamic industrial workpieces, calculate optimal 6-DoF grasp poses, and accurately assemble parts on dynamic fixtures.

sections.heading: The Challenge: Basic Manipulation Test (BMT)
sections.content: In RoboCup@Work, autonomous robots must execute mission orders communicated by a central referee box. As Team SWOT, our primary mission was conquering the Basic Manipulation Test (BMT). The BMT rigorously validates four essential capabilities: autonomous navigation, 3D object recognition, 6-DoF grasp planning, and precision component placement and rotation on varied industrial surfaces (wood, acrylic glass, turntables, shelving racks, and decoy clutter).

sections.heading: How the 3D Vision & Grasping Pipeline Works
sections.content: My perception and manipulation pipeline executed the following automated sequence in real-time:
list: Point Cloud Capture & PassThrough Filtering: Acquires raw point clouds from the eye-in-hand Intel RealSense D435i camera and crops non-relevant workspace boundaries.
Planar RANSAC Segmentation: Detects and subtracts worktable/shelf planes to isolate object candidate clusters from support surfaces.
Euclidean Cluster Extraction & Bounding Box Fitting: Segments individual workpieces and computes precise 3D centroid coordinates and surface normal vectors.
Grasp Pose Calculation & Collision-Free Approach: Computes 6-DoF gripper approach vectors, verifies joint limits on the UR3e arm, and executes smooth Cartesian trajectories via cartesian_ros_control.
Adaptive Force Grasping: Actuates the Robotiq Hand-E parallel gripper with calibrated force feedback to securely transport components to target drop-off zones.

sections.heading: Hardware Architecture: Team SWOT Platform
sections.content: Our mobile manipulator integrates industrial-grade embedded hardware:
list: Omnidirectional Mobile Base: Custom chassis by Evocortex GmbH equipped with Mecanum wheels, enabling holonomic sideways and diagonal translation in constrained factory lanes.
LiDAR Safety & Localization: Dual Sick TiM561 2D LiDAR scanners mounted diagonally to provide 360° environmental awareness for SLAM.
6-DoF Robotic Arm & End-Effector: Universal Robots UR3e collaborative arm with a Robotiq Hand-E precision parallel gripper, achieving a 50 cm payload reach.
3D Eye-in-Hand Vision: Intel RealSense D435i depth camera mounted directly on the gripper flange for point cloud capture.
Distributed Computing Cluster: Intel UP Xtreme host, NVIDIA Jetson TX2 for vision acceleration, and an onboard Lenovo ThinkPad.

sections.heading: Worldwide Results & Master's Thesis
sections.content: Competing against experienced international robotics teams, Team SWOT captured 4th place worldwide at RoboCup@Work 2021. The 3D vision algorithms and grasp planning software that I engineered also formed the core of my Master of Engineering thesis at FHWS, which was graded with highest honors (Grade 1.3 - ECTS Grade A).

oslo.title: Highlights & Architecture in Oslo, Norway
oslo.subtitle: Nordic Architecture, Fjord Landscapes, Maritime Heritage & Cultural Expeditions
oslo.author: Lukas Kraus

sections.heading: Impressions from the Nordic Fjord Capital
sections.content: The Norwegian capital of Oslo captivates visitors with its seamless fusion of cutting-edge modern architecture, pristine fjord landscapes, sustainable urban infrastructure, and rich cultural history.

gallery.name: Norsk Folkemuseum
gallery.desc: Traditional Norwegian wooden architecture and historic stave churches spanning the Middle Ages to modern times on the Bygdøy Peninsula.
gallery.caption: Norsk Folkemuseum — Traditional Timber Architecture

gallery.name: Fram Polar Ship Museum
gallery.desc: The epic history of Arctic and Antarctic explorations by Fridtjof Nansen, Otto Sverdrup, and Roald Amundsen aboard the historic vessel Fram.
gallery.caption: Fram Polar Ship Museum — Arctic Expeditions

gallery.name: Vigelandsanlegget
gallery.desc: The world's largest sculpture park by a single artist, featuring over 200 granite and bronze figures capturing the full cycle of human emotion and life.
gallery.caption: Vigeland Park — Granite and Bronze Sculptures

gallery.name: Oslo Opera House & Fjord Walk
gallery.desc: Walkable angled white Italian marble roof with panoramic fjord views, accompanied by open-air social Salsa and Bachata dancing on the waterfront.
gallery.caption: Oslo Opera House — Waterfront Architecture

dancing.title: The Dynamics of Partner Dancing: Social Connection & WSDC Competition
dancing.subtitle: Ballroom Standard & Latin, Salsa, Bachata, Kizomba, and Competitive West Coast Swing (WCS)
dancing.author: Lukas Kraus

sections.heading: A Lifelong Passion for Rhythm & Movement
sections.content: Balancing intense software engineering and mathematical problem-solving with the physical, dynamic realm of partner dancing has been one of my most rewarding pursuits. Partner dancing is not merely choreography; it is an intuitive real-time communication protocol between two dancers, driven by musicality, elasticity, and spatial awareness.

danceCards.title: Standard & Latin Ballroom
danceCards.desc: The foundation of partner movement: mastering rigid frame posture, swing-and-sway mechanics (Waltz, Quickstep, Tango), and sharp syncopated hip action (Cha-Cha, Rumba, Jive).

danceCards.title: Salsa & Bachata
danceCards.desc: Energetic social floor staples: Cuban and Cross-body Salsa turns, polyrhythmic musical timing, and sensual Dominican/Sensual Bachata body isolations.

danceCards.title: Kizomba
danceCards.desc: Deep grounded connection originating from Angola, focusing on subtle torso lead, smooth weight transfers, and intimate musical connection.

danceCards.title: West Coast Swing (WCS)
danceCards.desc: A linear, slotted dance characterized by elastic tension/compression, dynamic lead-follow improvisation, and adaptability to contemporary Pop, Blues, RnB, and Acoustic music.

sections.heading: WSDC Competition & The BaroqueSwing Milestone
sections.content: In the global West Coast Swing community, dancers compete under the official sanctioned guidelines of the World Swing Dance Council (WSDC) in randomized Jack & Jill competitions—where leaders and followers are randomly paired and dance to unannounced music.

sections.heading: Parallels Between Dancing & Software Engineering
sections.content: Much like architecting distributed systems or mobile manipulation pipelines in robotics, partner dancing relies on precise control loops:
list: Low-Latency Feedback: Continuous micro-adjustments through physical connection and visual cues.
Deterministic Frameworks with Dynamic Execution: Adhering to timing and slot rules while improvising freely to musical accents.
Empathy & Team Synergy: Enabling both partners to express their creativity seamlessly on the floor.
